subject: general
question: Which of the following is the greatest number that divides 59 and 133 and leaves 5 and 7 as respective remainders?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the **remainders** from the given numbers: (59 − 5) = 54 and (133 − 7) = 126.

Find the **HCF** of 54 and 126.

HCF(54, 126) = 18.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e2e54a19951bbc6c9d4d979d9c918e0d2b1e0122454a78316a1393dc26101a17.png] 

**Given:**

First number = 59, Remainder₁ = 5

Second number = 133, Remainder₂ = 7

**Calculations:**

⇒ First Required Number = 59 − 5 = 54

⇒ Second Required Number = 133 − 7 = 126

⇒ Prime factors of 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 2 × 3³

⇒ Prime factors of 126 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 = 2 × 3² × 7

⇒ HCF = 2 × 3² = 2 × 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF with remainders

To find the greatest number dividing a, b, c leaving remainders x, y, z, calculate HCF of (a−x), (b−y), and (c−z).

LCM with remainders

To find the least number which when divided by x, y, z leaves the same remainder r, calculate [LCM(x, y, z) + r].

Product Rule

For any two numbers, Product of numbers = HCF × LCM.</p
